h: Pinchas Awakens Teshuvah and Receives the Souls of Kehunah

p: פִּנְחָס בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר וְגוֹ׳ (בְּמִדְבַּר כה, יא)
in his being zealous with My zeal in their midst, etc.
הִנְנִי נוֹתֵן לוֹ אֶת בְּרִיתִי שָׁלוֹם
Behold, I give him My covenant of peace."
בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (חֵלֶק ג ריד, ב)
In the holy Zohar on this parshah (III 214b):
זְכָר נָא מִי הוּא נָקִי אָבָד
'Remember now, who that was innocent ever perished,
and where were the upright cut off?'"
what are they doing with Pinchas? etc.
For Pinchas was in the world, etc.
At the time Pinchas was zealous
when he saw the tribe of Shimon, etc.,
for he did not perish at that time, etc.;
'and where were the upright cut off':
these are the sons of Aharon, etc."
To understand the connection of the opening:
If so, when they were anointed
and Aharon merited the crown of kehunah,
Nadav and Avihu merited it too,
and for their generations after them;
so when Pinchas became a Kohen,
did he not take from their portion
and become a partner with them in the covenant of kehunah,
which belonged only to Aharon and his descendants?
that descendants of Pinchas would merit the high priesthood,
and the seed of Aharon who were anointed would lose;
and Hashem Yisbarach does not take back
And on this he brings this exposition:
and he was like one born anew;
and the souls of Nadav and Avihu entered him,
and they had had no children;
"for his descendants after him, a covenant of eternal kehunah,"
for they are actually the seed of Nadav and Avihu.
that at the time of the incident
לֹא נִזְכַּר שֵׁם אִישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל הַמּוּכֶּה
the name of the man of Yisrael who was struck was not mentioned,
nor the name of the Midianite woman,
which speaks of the greatness of Pinchas,
Now in the Midrash (Bamidbar Rabbah 21:3 and Tanchuma Pinchas 2):
"Just as the Holy One, blessed is He, takes pains
over the praise of the tzaddikim to publicize them,
so He takes pains over the disgrace of the wicked
It appears that it comes to settle this:
that here, where the tzaddik Pinchas is mentioned in praise,
that his real name was Shlumiel son of Tzurishaddai,
and he was called Zimri son of Salu
so what disgrace is publicized by this,
כֵּיוָן שֶׁלֹּא נִקְרָא מֵעוֹלָם בְּשֵׁם זֶה
since he was never called by this name?
וְשׁוּב הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְהַזְכִּיר שֵׁם זֶה
And further, it should have mentioned this name
at the time of the incident.
וְאָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
and Rabbi Yehudah ben Beseira said to Rabbi Akiva:
אַתָּה עָתִיד לִיתֵּן אֶת הַדִּין וְכוּלֵּי
you will have to give an accounting, etc.:
אַף דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא דָּרַשׁ גְּזֵרָה שָׁוָה
even though Rabbi Akiva expounded a gezeirah shavah,
only that Rabbi Yehudah ben Beseira
had not received that gezeirah shavah.
where there is no hint at all in the Torah
that Zimri is Shlumiel son of Tzurishaddai,
why did they expound in the Gemara (Sanhedrin 82b)
that he is Shlumiel son of Tzurishaddai,
and how many names he had?
3) It also needs to be understood:
"Shaul: that he lent himself to sin";
why was he called Shaul then,
because he lent himself to sin
after two hundred ten years in Egypt
and forty years in the Wilderness?
that he did a Canaanite deed;
two hundred fifty years before the deed?
ה) גַּם מַה שֶּׁדָּרְשׁוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה פ)
"The Canaanite woman: the son of Dinah,
who was violated by a Canaanite";
it is difficult: why did they mention in disgrace
Dinah, the righteous woman who was forced?
6) It also needs to be understood
why he was not called son of Shimon,
and why he was named after Dinah.
ז) גַּם מַה שֶּׁנִּקְרָא בֶּן סָלוּא
7) Also, that he is called son of Salu,
"that he brought to mind the sin of his family,"
that he caused it to be remembered and recounted;
and he cited from the expression (Iyov 28:16)
"it cannot be valued with the gold of Ophir,"
of the explanation of the term "hislia,"
and why he was not called by a name
ח) גַּם קוּשִׁית הַמַּהַרְשָׁ״א זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
8) Also the question of the Maharsha, of blessed memory:
לָמָּה לֹא דָּרְשׁוּ גַּם שֵׁם צוּרִישַׁדָּי
why did they not expound the name Tzurishaddai too,
as they expounded the name Salu
9) It also needs to be understood:
that Zimri and Kozbi did not cry out
for the members of his tribe to rescue them?
that he too was going to fulfill his desires;
but at the time of the act,
why did they not cry out?
And the Gemara counts this among the miracles.
how did the tribe of Shimon not kill him?
And this too is among the miracles.
But indeed in the holy Zohar it is explicit
that his soul flew from fright
when he saw the tribe of Shimon.
that what is said in the Torah (Bereishis 34:3),
"And his soul cleaved to Dinah, etc.,"
means that he cast impurity into her,
regarding a woman violated by a gentile.
And for this reason they said
that a woman violated by an uncircumcised man
harmed the son born from her
That is, although he was by then
and it did not enter his mind
רַק הִשְׁאִיל עַצְמוֹ עַל פִּי טָעוּתוֹ
he only lent himself through his error,
thinking that he needed to do so.
And indeed he had a sense
that she had some connection to him
at the end of the sefer Chesed L'Avraham,
that she was his destined mate,
only that he took her before her time);
that by this he would rectify the sin of his family.
For we find in the Gemara
that his tribe said to him:
were for the sin of idolatry,
that the worship of Peor was permitted,
since it is done in a degrading manner,
and the prohibition of a gentile woman had not yet been forbidden then;
and he wished by this to show
that there was no prohibition in the matter,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יְתַקֵּן עֲוֹן מִשְׁפַּחְתּוֹ
and through this he would rectify the sin of his family.
But this error came to him
because his mother had been violated by a Canaanite,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִדְבַּק בָּהּ הַזּוּהֲמָא
and through this the impurity clung to her,
and from her it clung to her offspring too,
עַד שֶׁעָשָׂה מַעֲשֵׂה כְּנַעַן לְפִי שָׁעָה
until he did a Canaanite deed for a time.

p: he brought thoughts of teshuvah into them,
into the entire tribe of Shimon,
and also into Zimri and Kozbi,
who was a reincarnation of Dinah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָאֲרִ״י הַקָּדוֹשׁ זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
as the holy Arizal, of blessed memory, wrote.
And for this reason Zimri and Kozbi were silent,
and it was good in their eyes
so that it would be an atonement for them.
And likewise the tribe of Shimon were silent,
because they had thoughts of teshuvah in their hearts.
and that is why it counted it
among the miracles done for Pinchas.
And this is what it says:
in his being zealous with My zeal in their midst";
and the word "in their midst" is superfluous
for it should have said "against them."
that he brought the zeal of Hashem into their midst too,
that is, into the heart of Zimri and Kozbi
הִנְנִי נוֹתֵן לוֹ אֶת בְּרִיתִי שָׁלוֹם
Behold, I give him My covenant of peace,"
for he merited the attribute of Yosef,
upon the tribe of Shimon and their prince.
And this is what is expounded there:
"that he brought to mind the sin of his family,"
in the sense of "comparable to fine gold":
for by his sin he wished to beautify the sin of his family,
that it was permitted to them,
and that they had no right
to judge capital cases against them.
(And in truth he "raised up the sin of his family"
in that Pinchas brought into them
thoughts of teshuvah in the tribe of Shimon;
it turns out that through Zimri
the sin of the whole tribe, who did teshuvah.)
And it concludes, "And what was his name?"
for the name is the essence of life:
"peace" is the attribute of Yosef HaTzaddik,
and "El" is the aspect of Knesses Yisrael
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק א ח, א
this is the glory of the bride, who is called El");
and it corresponds to the Name El Shaddai,
that is, that he bestows upon Knesses Yisrael.
צוּרִי הוּא עַל שֵׁם כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל
along the lines of what is written
שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִבָּן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל וְכוּלֵּי
that the Holy One, blessed is He, is the heart of Yisrael? etc.
'The Rock of my heart and my portion is God forever.'"
אֲנִי ה׳ שׁוֹכֵן בְּתוֹךְ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל (בְּמִדְבַּר לה, לד)
"I am Hashem Who dwells in the midst of the Children of Yisrael" (Bamidbar 35:34).
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג יא, ב)
which is the aspect of the tzaddik:
אֶת הָאֱלֹהִים אֲנִי יָרֵא (בְּרֵאשִׁית מב, יח)
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א ה, ב)
along the lines of what is written (Zohar I 5b):
And "the tzaddik is the foundation of the world" (Mishlei 10:25):
כִּי כֹל בַּשָּׁמַיִם וּבָאָרֶץ (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א כט, יא)
"for all that is in heaven and on earth" (Divrei HaYamim I 29:11),
that it holds fast to heaven and earth
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק א לא, סוֹף עַמּוּד א)
that is, he bestows upon Knesses Yisrael;
and this is the essence of his name and his life.
But for a time he erred
and lent himself for a time to sin;
and Pinchas immediately brought into him
and he accepted his death upon himself,
וְאַחַר כָּךְ אָמַר הַכָּתוּב (בְּמִדְבַּר כה, יג)
"And it shall be for him and his descendants after him
a covenant of eternal kehunah, etc.":
for he merited the crown of kehunah
for himself and for the generations;
"because he was zealous for his God, etc.,"
and he gave his life over the zeal of Hashem,
and his soul flew from fright,
and the souls of Nadav and Avihu entered him;
and through this he merited the kehunah
And therefore the verse mentions here:
"And the name of the man of Yisrael, etc.,"
was the prince of the tribe of Shimon,
וְעַל יְדֵי כֵן פָּרְחָה נִשְׁמָתוֹ שֶׁל פִּנְחָס
and through this he merited the kehunah
And it mentions their names for the reason of
"and it shall be for him and his descendants after him
And this is what is expounded in the holy Zohar (III 217a)
זְכוֹר נָא מִי הוּא נָקִי אָבָד
"Remember now, who that was innocent ever perished":
that he did not perish when his soul flew;
"and where were the upright cut off":
what had been lost in their lifetime.
And with this we will understand
what is written in the holy Zohar (III 221b):
and not 'who was struck, who was struck,' etc.;
He did not want to mention Pinchas
in connection with killing a person, etc.;
before He raised him to be Kohen Gadol,
And it is difficult to understand:
that it was written in a veiled way,
when in truth Pinchas killed them,
and he is not fit to be Kohen Gadol?
may the memory of the holy tzaddik be for a blessing
for the life of the World to Come,
that he did not say them in their name, etc.:
אֵין אוֹמְרִים דְּבַר הֲלָכָה מִשְּׁמוֹ וְכוּלֵּי
a word of halachah is not said in his name, etc.
What is 'And he poured them out to Hashem'?
That he said them in the name of the tradition."
And why is this the punishment
לְמוֹסֵר עַצְמוֹ לָמוּת עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
of one who gives himself to death for words of Torah,
that they are not said in his name?
And our holy Rebbe, of blessed memory, said
that this is not as a punishment;
רַק כֵּיוָן שֶׁמָּסַר עַצְמוֹ לָמוּת עַל זֶה
rather, since he gave himself over to death for it,
he no longer has a connection
rather it is from Hashem Yisbarach;
they say them in the name of the tradition.
And this is the meaning of
"And he poured them out to Hashem":
that it is only from the side of Hashem Yisbarach
and not from his own power.
for himself and for the generations
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר תַּחַת אֲשֶׁר קִנֵּא וְגוֹ׳
as it says, "because he was zealous, etc.,"
the killing is not called by his name,
כִּי אִם עַל שֵׁם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
but by the Name of Hashem Yisbarach.
And this is why it says "who was struck, who was struck"
that he was struck by Hashem Yisbarach.
And likewise "and the name of the woman who was struck"
is also in a veiled way,
for it was by Hashem Yisbarach,
"And he poured them out to Hashem," as mentioned above.
